claims.claim: take guarantees nothing about which records it returns unless the data is sorted; bin rounds down; summarize on empty input with a by clause returns no rows; make-series assigns a default to absent values.
KQL database retention defaults to 3,650 days, maximum 36,500, minimum one day, unlimited option; caching policy controls data kept in the hot cache.
OneLake availability can be enabled per database or table.

concept_html:
An eventhouse holds one or more KQL databases, built for high-volume, time-stamped data such as telemetry, logs and clickstreams. You query them with the Kusto Query Language (KQL): a pipeline of operators joined by |, read top to bottom.

telemetry_raw
| where event_time > ago(1h)
| where event_type == "reading"
| summarize avg_rpm = avg(rpm), n = count() by vehicle_id, bin(event_time, 5m)
  • Put where filters first, especially on time. They cut the data every later operator touches.
  • ago(1h) is one hour before now. bin(event_time, 5m) rounds times down to five-minute buckets.
  • summarize ... by aggregates per group.

Three KQL behaviours catch people out (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026):

  • take returns arbitrary rows. There is no guarantee which records come back, and repeated runs can differ, unless the data is sorted. For "the latest 10", use top 10 by event_time desc.
  • summarize leaves gaps. A five-minute bin with no events produces no row, so a chart draws a straight line across an outage. make-series ... default = 0 ... step 5m fills missing bins.
  • Empty input. summarize count() without by returns one row. With by, empty input returns no rows at all.

Data policies are set per database or table. The retention policy removes old data automatically. The default is 3,650 days, the maximum 36,500, the minimum one day, and you can set it to unlimited. The caching policy decides how much recent data stays in the hot cache on local SSD: faster queries, higher cost. Set retention from the use: raw telemetry kept 90 days, daily aggregates kept for years.

Turn on OneLake availability for a database or table to expose its data as Delta in OneLake, so Spark and the SQL analytics endpoint can read it without a copy.

lines: | where event_time > ago(1h)
| where event_type == "reading"
| make-series avg_rpm = avg(rpm) default = 0 on event_time step 5m by vehicle_id
| where event_time > ago(15m)
| top 10 by event_time desc

title: Eventhouse and KQL for time-series questions
why_html: An on-call dashboard showed the "latest readings" from a KQL query ending in | take 10. During an incident, the panel showed readings from two hours earlier, mixed with current ones, and the engineer concluded the sensor had recovered. It had not. take returned arbitrary rows. top 10 by event_time desc would have shown the true latest readings.
